text: This code of conduct governs the environment of Minnesota Roller Derby (MNRD). It was created not because we anticipate bad behavior, but because we believe that articulating our values and obligations to one another reinforces respect among the league and it provides the league with clear avenues to correct our culture when it ever strays off course.
While not intended to be an all-inclusive list, the examples below represent behavior that is considered unacceptable for MNRD member organizations and their communities.
Failure to adhere to this code of conduct may result in disciplinary action up to and including permanent expulsion from the MNRD.
Theft or inappropriate removal/possession of property.
Intimidation, verbal abuse or harassment, sexual harassment or assault, and/or physical violence beyond the normal scope of game play.
Making maliciously false statements about athletes, members, coaching staff, officials, volunteers, administrators, registrants, and other MNRD participants.
Purposefully and willfully violating MNRD policies.
Purposefully and willfully violating safety or health rules.

Participating in any illegal activity during practice, bouts, or any league sponsored activities, to include any use of drugs, or alcohol that can endanger spectators, fellow teammates, opposing skaters, or the skater themselves.

Bullying, including through league policies, that purposefully enables exclusion based on race, ethnicity, religion, color, national origin, age, disability (physical or mental), sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, parental status, pregnancy status, marital status, political affiliation, military and veteran status, as well as mental health status, socioeconomic status or background, neuro(a)typicality, or physical appearance.

Social media posts of abusive, harmful, or harassing content that attack a person's or group's race, ethnicity, religion, color, national origin, age, disability (physical or mental), sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, parental status, pregnancy status, marital status, political affiliation, military and veteran status, as well as mental health status, socioeconomic status or background, neuro(a)typicality, or physical appearance.

While a progressive coaching and disciplinary plan will be followed the majority of the time, the MNRD can, at its discretion, bypass the Code of Conduct and immediately suspend or expel athletes, members, coaching staff, officials, volunteers, administrators, registrants, and other participants if the circumstances warrant.
Additionally, MNRD as an organization does not endorse the inherently racist structures of our society and works to identify and change what's possible within its influence.
Every member of the league is empowered to identify where those racist systems are upheld in our interactions and to act to make changes that correct those racist structures.
Any member who acts to uphold those racist structures would be considered counter to the goals of the league.
